title: Fix the Method That Can't Modify a Primitive
description: The program should double a number using a helper method.
expectedBehavior: After calling doubleValue(x), x should be 10.
actualProblem: Java passes primitives (like int) by value, so n inside doubleValue is a separate copy of x. Modifying n has no effect on the original x back in main, which still prints 5.
explanation: Since primitives can't be modified through a method parameter, the method must return the new value and the caller must assign it back to the variable it wants updated.
